newsitem.title: USA: Dixie Yarns sees Q4 $14 mln charge.
newsitem.headline: Dixie Yarns sees Q4 $14 mln charge.

text.p: Dixie Yarns Inc said on Thursday it would take a non-cash, after-tax charge of about $14 million on its fourth quarter, mostly for the write-down of its Tarboro, N.C. yarn spinning facility.

The company said it decided to exit the commodity open-end cottom markets served by this operation, to put the facility up for sale and to discontinue certain other businesses as part of its strategy to reposition Dixie Yarns into a more consumer driven company focused on high-margin products.
Dixie Yarns makes floorcovering and textile products for specialty markets. Its textiles products include yarns, knit fabrics and apparel.
The company also said it completed the acquisition of the business and operating assets of Danube Carpet Mills Inc, a unit of Shelter Components Corp Inc, for about $18.2 million cash.
The price was $6.8 million less than previously announced because the seller retained accounts receivable and the sale of a portion of the real estate was deferred, Dixie said.

Dixie's Chairman and Chief Executive Daniel Frierson said: "The acquisition of Danube and the Company's strategy to reduce spinning of commodity yarn products and expand its apparel business will increase the company's sales of consumable products."
He said this strategy improved gross margins and reduced selling, general and administrative expenses in 1996, and that the company expected these these trends to continue in 1997.
Danube, headquartered in Ft. Oglethorpe, Ga., antipates sales of about $75 million in 1996, the company said.
